title: Effectiveness of Suicide Prevention Programmes and Factors Accounting for 50% Rise in Suicide Deaths Among Adults aged 30 to 39
what_it_is: Effectiveness of Suicide Prevention Programmes and Factors Accounting for 50% Rise in Suicide Deaths Among Adults aged 30 to 39

sections.label: Suicide prevention strategy effectiveness
sections.summary: An MP asks about the effectiveness of suicide prevention for youth and men, and how the Government plans to address the findings.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of the effectiveness and adequacy of suicide prevention strategy and programmes, particularly (i) for youth, given that suicide has remained the leading cause of death among those aged 10 to 29 for seven consecutive years and (ii) for men, who account for the majority of suicide deaths; and (b) how does the Government plan to address these findings.

sections.label: Singapore suicide rate comparison
sections.summary: Singapore's suicide rate is generally lower than other developed economies, with an increase noted among those aged 30 to 39 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Overall, Singapore’s suicide rate is generally lower compared to other developed economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We note the increase in suicides among those aged 30 to 39 in 2024, following a relatively stable trend in the preceding years.

sections.label: Mental resilience and help-seeking
sections.summary: Strengthening mental resilience and encouraging early help-seeking are key to suicide prevention, implemented through the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Strengthening mental resilience and encouraging early help-seeking are therefore key to suicide prevention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: These are being implemented through the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sections.label: Provisional versus eventual statistics
sections.summary: Advocates say the wait is challenging, with a 35% to 40% difference between provisional statistics and eventual ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But advocates and also people who are active in the space have shared that this has been quite challenging, especially in the wait.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe the numbers show a 35% to 40% difference between the provisional statistics and the eventual ones, and these have been uptakes.

sections.label: Timely publication of figures
sections.summary: Figures are published timely despite being provisional to ensure transparency, with a time lag because provisional numbers are based on confirmed suicides at publication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The reason why we publish the figures in a timely manner, even though those might be provisional and would be updated later on, is to ensure there is transparency; that there is in enough information out there – for the purpose of transparency, for us to make decisions and to understand the trends and understand how we can better support those who are in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The reason why there is a time lag between the provisional numbers and the ones that are to be updated later on is because the provisional number of deaths reported in the annual report on Registration of Births and Deaths are based on those confirmed to be suicides at the time of the publication of the report.

sections.label: Men majority of suicide deaths
sections.summary: For many years, men have made up the majority of suicide deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For many years, men have made up the majority of suicide deaths.

sections.label: Holistic approach to suicide prevention
sections.summary: The passage states a holistic approach is taken to reduce stigma, improve suicide literacy, and help others recognise distress and connect someone to help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But we cannot design a system that depends only on someone putting up their hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, we are taking a holistic approach: making sure to reduce stigma to improve suicide literacy, but also to help families, friends, colleagues and communities to recognise distress and connect someone to help.
